s1.syndrome_frame: Acute onset of abnormal posturing and movement disorder following medication change
salient_findings: Bouts of extremely stiff, nonpainful neck
Involuntary posturing with head, neck, and spine arched backward
Conjugate deviation of the eyes upward or laterally
key_facts: 19-year-old female student
Admitted with grade III dyspnea
Prescribed diuretics and aspirin post-surgery
Started new medication at low dose (25 mg per day) for two days
Dose increased to 25 mg twice daily on the third day
Readmitted on the same evening after discharge
Subpulmonic ventricular septal defect
Severe aortic regurgitation due to right coronary cusp prolapse
Dilated left ventricle with ejection fraction of 40%
Mild aortic regurgitation post-repair
Normal blood chemistry and electrolyte levels

shortlist.label: Acute Dystonic Reaction
shortlist.why_kept: Sudden onset of dystonic posturing after medication change

shortlist.label: Tardive Dyskinesia
shortlist.why_kept: Involuntary movements and posturing following medication use

shortlist.label: Antipsychotic-Induced Dystonia
shortlist.why_kept: Dystonic reaction potentially caused by new medication

shortlist.label: Status Dystonicus
shortlist.why_kept: Life-threatening dystonic state requiring immediate attention

raw.rationale: The patient's symptoms of an extremely stiff, nonpainful neck, conjugate deviation of the eyes, and involuntary posturing appeared after starting a new medication, which is a common trigger for acute dystonic reactions.

rejected.label: Tardive Dyskinesia
rejected.why: Typically occurs after long-term use of antipsychotic medications, which is not indicated in this case.

rejected.label: Dystonic Storm
rejected.why: Characterized by intense and frequent episodes of dystonia, which is not described in the vignette.

rejected.label: Antipsychotic-Induced Dystonia
rejected.why: There is no mention of the patient taking antipsychotic medications.

rejected.label: Status Dystonicus
rejected.why: A life-threatening condition with continuous and severe dystonic posturing, which is not described in the vignette.
